chose: never keep a refusal whose words carry a tsserver assertion (Debug Failure), and never one with a transient protocol code (-32800, -32801, -32802, -32002); keep every other error the server returned, as broad, while the tree is unchanged
over: keeping every RpcError, Debug Failure included, since it arrives as code 1 like a stack overflow
because: a Debug Failure is tsserver asserting on its own state, which follows the session's history: what was opened and asked before. A later reading of the same tree asks only what is not kept, through a fresh or a warm server, so it does not replay that history and may be answered; keeping it would leave the file unanswered on a tree a fresh server can read. Not keeping it costs the spawn only for that rare case, while the deterministic refusal the PR was for (Maximum call stack size exceeded) is still kept
